name: God Helmet classic (Persinger 2-phase)
origin: Persinger & Koren (Laurentian University) sensed-presence protocol; home version by Todd Murphy (Shiva God Helmet software)
summary: Persinger and Koren's two-phase procedure in Todd Murphy's Shiva God Helmet version: 30 min of the "modulated 40 Hz chirp" cycling around four coils on the RIGHT temporal lobe only, then an abrupt switch to 30 min of the amygdala burst-firing signal cycling on both temporal lobes. Phase 1 can cause fear; press Skip to go straight to phase 2.
notes: Murphy reports that the lab ran phase 1 for about 30 min before the abrupt switch; his Shiva version runs 30 + 30 min (as here) or 20 + 20 min. Four coils sit in a cross on each temporal lobe (about FT7, C5, TP7, T9 and FT8, C6, TP8, T10; the site names are an inference; Murphy says the lab helmet's two top coils and the centre coil between the four on each side are no longer used). Phase 1 drives only the right cross, stepping counter-clockwise; phase 2 drives both crosses, clockwise on the left and counter-clockwise on the right, as the session page text says and as Collins 2014 describes the Shiva 4+4 helmet in Persinger's lab (an image caption on Murphy's session list says clockwise on the right). Viewed side by side both run top, back, bottom, front (an inference). Murphy gives no step time, only "a fraction of a second" per cycle; 125 ms per coil (0.5 s per cycle) is an inference. Both signals are proprietary. The "modulated 40 Hz chirp" (the vendor: a modulated 40 Hz signal whose gaps grow longer, with Fibonacci-varied amplitude and gaps; one vendor page says it "does not change in tone", another shows a chirp whose frequency falls) is approximated by a frequency sweep falling from 40 to 6 Hz on 3-ms points, 2.5 s on and 1.5 s off (837 points of 3 ms every 4 s, after the lab's frequency-modulated 'Thomas' pattern: 837 values every 4 s, Dixon & Persinger 2001; 3-ms points over the right hemisphere, Tiller & Persinger 2002); the 40 Hz modulation and the amplitude variation are not reproduced. Changed after the primary-source check: the amygdala signal now has the length a Laurentian thesis gives for the Shiva software's own "amygdaloid signal, normal speed", 289 points of 3 ms (0.87 s) with 4 s between cycles (Collins 2014), approximated by the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz); it was 230 points (0.69 s), the length of the lab's own Burst-X file (Carniello 2020), which the lab played once every 3-4 s. The lab's own protocol (Saroka 2015) is 30 min of the frequency-modulated Thomas pattern over both temporoparietal regions, then 30 min of Burst-X (persinger-saroka-2015-sensed-presence). When Persinger's lab tested Shiva's 4+4 helmet (coils 5 cm apart vertically and 8 cm horizontally, 1-2 uT, 20-min primer and target phases, 24 people), only right-frontal high-beta rose (Collins 2014). The Shiva software plays phase 1 10 % louder than the user setting, so phase 2 runs at level 0.91. Murphy calls phase 1 "somewhat unpleasant for many people" ("women seem to be more prone") and warns against making it an endurance contest; if anger or irritability appears during or after phase 2, never repeat the session. Not for people prone to anxiety or with epilepsy, migraine, brain injury, a psychiatric diagnosis or medication; no drugs or other mind machines. Persinger, quoted by Murphy, put visions of Christ or God at about 20 of some 2000 lab subjects. Independent double-blind tests found no effect of the field (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012).
setting: Dark, silent room ("silence, not just quiet"), blindfold, eyes closed, reclined; relax without meditating or falling asleep. Lab sessions ran mostly between midnight and 4 am in an acoustic chamber that was also a Faraday cage. For experiences during the session Murphy advises geomagnetic quiet (K 0-2). A helper can press Skip if phase 1 becomes frightening, so you stay in the dark.
schedule: At most weekly, never on consecutive days; six sessions, then a 21-day break; don't mix with other Shiva or Shakti sessions in the same weeks. Murphy advises starting with other sessions before this one.
